To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the critical population size for branching process approximation of the probability of extinction of an infectious disease in a single patch is a function of the transition rates of the model.

(a) the probability of disease outbreak is approximated using branching process approximation, (b) branching process approximation is accurate for a wide range of population sizes at the disease free state, (c) branching process approximation can be used to determine the threshold of disease persistence, (d) the threshold of disease invasion is the basic reproduction number, and (e) the threshold of persistence is not the basic reproduction number.

(1) the probability of extinction for the one patch model can be approximated accurately using a branching process approximation when the initial number of infected individuals is small; (2) the probability of outbreak in a one patch model with a more realistic force infection can be approximated using a branching process; (3) the critical size for the branching process approximation is estimated to be approximately 1000 individuals; (4) the critical size is not affected by the transition rates of the model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and analysis of stochastic models of disease spread.
the analysis of stochastic models of the dynamics of Infectious Salmon Anaemia virus in a single patch and in two patches.
the development of stochastic models to study the effects of random fluctuation on disease dynamics in a population.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the critical size for branching process approximation to accurately predict the probability of disease persistence is dependent on the force of infection and the transition rate of the system.
for the single patch system the branching process approximation is a good approximation of the probability of disease extirpation if there are greater than 50 individuals at the DFE.

the branching process approximation of the probability of extinction for a single patch model is accurate when the number of susceptibles at the disease free equilibria is greater than the critical population size.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the probability of disease outbreak in the one patch system is highly sensitive to the initial condition and the probability of outbreak decreases with decreasing initial condition.
the branching process approximation is an effective tool for approximating the probability of extinction for the one patch and two patch stochastic systems.
the probability of disease outbreak is dependent on both the basic reproduction number and the size of the susceptible population at the disease free state.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the probability of extinction for the one patch deterministic model is not a good approximation of the probability of extinction in the stochastic model for small population sizes.
for a given system, the probability of extinction depends on the initial conditions and that the probability of outbreak can be approximated with a branching process approximation.
for a given set of transition rates the probability of disease persistence is a function of the initial number of susceptible individuals.
